newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT-Boost weightings in Israeli banks.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Boost weightings in Israeli banks.

text.p: Sahar Securities and Investments, a Tel Aviv brokerage, said on Wednesday it had initiated coverage of three more Israeli banks and recommended investors increase their weighting in bank shares.
Sahar said it was rating Bank Leumi a buy and both Israel Discount Bank and First International of Israel a hold. To date, Sahar had only covered Bank Hapoalim, which it rated a buy.
Sahar said it assigned Hapoalim and Leumi, Israel's two biggest commercial banks, a buy rating because they had raised earnings over the last five years at a faster pace than their competitors.

"This improvement occurred to a far lesser extent at the two smaller banks -- Discount and First International -- despite the fact that they posted sharper growth in credit to the public, i.e.their profit margins sharply eroded," Sahar said.

"During the past several years, bank shares have performed better than the Mishtanim index " Sahar said. "We attribute this to the fact that return on equity in the banking sector has risen, while return in the industrial sector has declined."
It said bank earnings would remain strong in 1997 and 1998, continuing the trend of the previous five years.

The banks trade at a lower prospective price-to-earnings ratio than the overall market, Sahar said, while earnings per share at the banks are not expected to grow any slower, and perhaps even faster, than the overall market.
